verdicts.why: B's three pills are exactly the reader's own three interests and every article sits under the right one. A offers finer sub-topics, but its 'industrial revolution' pill omits two of the five articles, 'roads' mixes a railway post in with Rome, 'railways' holds a child-labour report, and 'Royal Society' is a narrow name for the science group.

Narrow call. B has the right three concepts but files the railways post under Roman Empire and leaves it out of Industrial Revolution, a glaring error; A has no single error that bad but two wrong inclusions, an incomplete umbrella pill and more arbitrary labels, so B's better labels just outweigh it.

Same three labels in both, but A's membership is exactly right while B puts the railways post under Roman Empire, drops it from Industrial Revolution and adds the steam engine piece to History of Science.
